claim: NVMe device self-test capability is optional per-drive: on an Intel SSDPEKKF256G7L (600p series), 'nvme intel-id-ctrl -H' shows 'Device Self-test Not Supported' (oacs bit [4:4] = 0, edstt = 0, dsto = 0) despite the drive reporting 'health: healthy' — so an agent cannot assume smartctl self-tests work on all NVMe drives.
stance_target: the assumption that SMART self-test commands are uniformly available across NVMe fleet hardware; agents must feature-detect (oacs/dsto bits) and fall back to controller health log polling
scope_conditions: Intel SSD 600p series NVMe (SSDPEKKF256G7L, fw 121P); consumer NVMe drives generally; capability varies by vendor
quoted_support: It seems that self-test are not supported: #nvme intel-id-ctrl /dev/nvme0 -H ... oacs : 0x7 [4:4] : 0 Device Self-test Not Supported ... edstt : 0 dsto : 0 ... health : healthy

claim: Per Arch forum moderator V1del: smartctl supports NVMe drives in recent versions; nvme-cli's nvme-smart-log / nvme-device-self-test / nvme-self-test-log are the relevant commands; vendor-specific nvme-cli commands may expose additional information; SMART checks and self-tests are usually doable during normal operation while fsck needs an unmounted filesystem.
stance_target: agent NVMe health monitoring can run non-destructively on live, mounted root devices using smartctl or nvme-cli without unmounting
scope_conditions: smartmontools 7.0+; nvme-cli; Linux 5.x era; capabilities depend on exact drive model
quoted_support: Smartctl has support for NVME drives in recent times ... Alternatively see the following nvme cli commands' manpages ... In general all of the tools you list here are non-destructive by default ... smartctls and self tests should usually be doable during normal operation. fsck should be done unmounted

claim: The Intel 600p in the thread reports warning/critical composite temperature thresholds of 70°C / 80°C (wctemp 343K, cctemp 353K) and five power states ranging from 9.00W operational to 0.005W non-operational — temperature thresholds are queryable per-drive from identify data.
stance_target: agent can derive per-drive thermal warning thresholds from NVMe identify-controller data rather than hardcoding
quoted_support: wctemp : 343 cctemp : 353 ... ps 0 : mp:9.00W operational ... ps 4 : mp:0.0050W non-operational
